newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bel-20,close to dizzying heights,to take breather.
newsitem.headline: Bel-20,close to dizzying heights,to take breather.

text.p: The Bel-20 share index .BFX chalked up a 0.75 percent gain on Wednesday on the back of a fresh fall in long-term interest rates, a dollar holding steady at firmer levels and a higher Wall Street .DJI.
The Bel-20 ended up 13.55 points at 1,823.91. With a session high of 1,825.16 the index did not come close to the 1996 high of 1,829.85 and some dealers doubted it would in the near term.

"We are heading for a consolidation after the good gains of the recent days," said a trader. Another said that the downtrend in interest rates, a major driving force this year, was coming to an end. "There is not much more scope," he said.

"Momentum is sliding," said a trader, adding he saw the index moving in a range between 1,800 and 1,830 points until the end of the year. Some chartists put resistance at 1,825/30, but others are aiming for a record-breaking 1,850.

The bourse also gained on relief U.S. elections maintained the governmental status quo. Dealers said investors, naturally conservative, were pleased the U.S. electorate left Bill Clinton in the White House, but Republicans in control of Congress.
Analysts said that set-up would help ensure there would be no Democrat spending spree, keeping inflation and the U.S. budget deficit in check.

Among individual stocks, U.S.-exposed Delhaize stood out, gaining on the back of dollar stability and expectations of instant profit contributions from a recent U.S. purchase by its U.S. Food Lion unit.
With a 2.5 percent rise to 1,845 francs Delhaize led the market, followed closely by Bel-20 heavy-weight PetroFina.

The share saw more pronounced gains after Tuesday's lukewarm reaction to a company announcement 1996 profit would rise to around 15 billion Belgian francs from 12.3 billion in 1995. PetroFina had a 1995 group net profit, less minorities, of 11.6 billion francs.
The energy share was up 1.0 percent at 9,760 francs.
Bank stocks advanced on the back of falling capital market rates. Generale Bank outperformed the index, adding 0.9 percent at 11,250.

But BBL lagged behind, firming only 10 francs at 6,470, with one trader saying some players were switching out of the share to create room in their portfolios for the impending initial public offering of Gemeentekrediet shares.
Chemicals and drug share UCB put on 0.9 percent at 69,750 francs in thin trade. One trader cited index basket purchases and the dollar.
